# nullplatform_application_type (Resource)

The application_type resource manages a nullplatform Application Type: a kind of application an organization defines, with the fields its applications carry and the places it can be used.

`terraform destroy` deletes the type, which gives its name back. The platform refuses the delete while an application of the type exists or a template belongs to it: delete those first, or move the templates to another type. To stop new applications from taking a type that is still in use, set `status = "inactive"` instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    nullplatform = {
      source = "nullplatform/nullplatform"
    }
  }
}

provider "nullplatform" {}

variable "account_nrn" {
  description = "NRN of the account that owns the application type, e.g. organization=1:account=2"
  type        = string
}

variable "namespace_id" {
  description = "ID of the namespace that owns the application"
  type        = number
}

# The schema is the form the platform shows when an application of this type
# is created, with the fields in the order written here. It is JSON in a
# heredoc (or file("agent.schema.json")) and not jsonencode(), which would
# put the keys of every object in alphabetical order.
resource "nullplatform_application_type" "agent" {
  nrn         = var.account_nrn
  name        = "AI Agent"
  description = "An agent that runs a model on a schedule or on demand"

  # Where the type can be used. Left out, it is the type's own NRN.
  visible_to = [var.account_nrn]

  schema = <<-JSON
    {
      "type": "object",
      "required": ["model"],
      "properties": {
        "model": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Model",
          "enum": ["small", "large"]
        },
        "autonomy": {
          "type": "string",
          "title": "Autonomy",
          "enum": ["low", "high"],
          "default": "low"
        },
        "max_steps": {
          "type": "integer",
          "title": "Maximum steps",
          "minimum": 1
        }
      }
    }
  JSON
}

# An application of the type: its attributes are checked against the schema.
resource "nullplatform_application" "support_bot" {
  name                = "support-bot"
  namespace_id        = var.namespace_id
  application_type_id = nullplatform_application_type.agent.id

  # Keeps the application on the type's latest schema: when the schema above
  # changes, the same apply moves the application to the snapshot it cuts.
  # Left out, the application stays on the snapshot it was created on.
  application_type_snapshot_id = nullplatform_application_type.agent.last_snapshot_id

  attributes = jsonencode({
    model     = "large"
    autonomy  = "low"
    max_steps = 20
  })
}

# A template that only applications of the type can start from.
resource "nullplatform_technology_template" "agent_starter" {
  name                = "Agent starter"
  url                 = "https://github.com/my-org/agent-starter"
  application_type_id = nullplatform_application_type.agent.id

  provider_config = {
    repository = "agent-starter"
  }

  components {
    type    = "language"
    id      = "python"
    version = "3.12"
  }
}

output "application_type_snapshot" {
  description = "The snapshot that holds the current schema; it changes when the schema does"
  value       = nullplatform_application_type.agent.last_snapshot_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the application type, up to 120 characters. No two types visible in the same organization share a name. Renaming a type does not change its `slug`.
- `nrn` (String) The NRN that owns the application type, for example `organization=1:account=2`. It cannot be changed: a different NRN is a different type, so changing it deletes this one and creates another, which the platform refuses while applications or templates use this one.
- `schema` (String) The JSON Schema (draft-07, 2019-09 or 2020-12, root `type` `object`) that the `attributes` of an application of this type must pass, as a JSON string. The platform shows its properties as a form **in the order they are written**, so that order is kept: the properties are sent in the order written, and reordering them is a change. `jsonencode()` writes the keys of every object in alphabetical order; to choose the order, write the schema as JSON with `file()` or a heredoc. A change of schema cuts a new snapshot (`last_snapshot_id`); applications stay on the snapshot they are on until they are moved.

### Optional

- `description` (String) What the application type is for, up to 255 characters.
- `status` (String) `active` or `inactive`. Only an active type can be given to a new application; the applications that already have the type keep it either way. The platform creates a type `active` when this is not set.
- `visible_to` (Set of String) The NRNs where the application type can be used: an application created at or below one of them may take it. When not set, the platform makes the type visible at its own `nrn`. It cannot be an empty list.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_snapshot_id` (String) The ID of the snapshot that holds the current `schema`. New applications are created on it. It changes whenever `schema` does.
- `slug` (String) The slug of the application type, made from its name when it is created. It never changes.
